answer: A ring signature hides the signer among a ring, and the key image tags any second signature from the same key. Signing 345 times needs 345 distinct keys, since a reused key image links the signatures together. Key images are recorded on-chain, and a repeated image proves the same key signed twice. The glacier check runs in the open: 345 fakes pay the full price 345 times, one honest agent pays once, and the signal trail in the ledger makes the tide cost visible to everyone.
